$comment: What a client keeps of one person in a SessionStorage, and when it is read, written and deleted, as every SDK must do it. A client keeps the answers of the queries protocol/specs/src/client/refresh.json marks `persisted`, and where its stream was, under keys that name the knowledge base and the person the gateway said its token is (protocol/specs/src/session/stored.json, `lastEventIdKeyPrefix` and `cacheKeyPrefix`). The person's key is recorded in the stored sign-in (`storedSession`'s `personKey`) once the gateway names them. `people` are the people the parts name, each by a did and the key it makes. `keys`: each row is a knowledge base and a person, and the key of every persisted query, in the order refresh.json lists them, and of the stream's places; a runner fails unless its persisted queries are exactly those, in that order, and it makes every key. `signOut`: what a registry's sign-out of `kb-a` deletes. Before each row, storage holds every key of `signOutStorage`, and `signedIn` says what kb-a's stored sign-in is: `named`, a sign-in whose personKey is jo's; `unnamed`, one with no personKey; `none`, nothing stored. `open` is whether kb-a is active when it is signed out, with its client kept for jo; a runner may stand in for that client a session whose closing writes a value under jo's `resource` key, as a client closing with a save pending could (protocol/contract/CACHE-SEMANTICS.md, B17). `removes` is `person` when the sign-out deletes every key of the person the stored sign-in names on kb-a, the stream's and every persisted query's, whether or not each holds anything, and `nothing` when it deletes none; every other key of `signOutStorage` holds what it held. The sign-out deletes only after the client has closed, so whatever its closing does, no key the row removes holds anything afterwards. `startup`: a session of kb-a made by a registry over storage that holds `startupStorage`, whose gateway answers who the token is as `gateway` says (`names`: jo, with `whoAmI`; `unreachable`: no answer). A read of a resource the gateway is asked for is answered with that resource named `fresh`. `first` is what the client gives for res-2 when it is asked before the gateway has answered who the token is, and `then` what it gives for res-1 when it is asked after, res-1's scope not having been subscribed to before: `kept`, the value `startupStorage` keeps (given at once, then revalidated as B18 says), or `fresh`, the gateway's answer (nothing kept was read). `recorded` is the personKey the stored sign-in holds once the gateway has answered, null for none. `place` is the event id the stream resumes res-1's scope from when it is subscribed to after the gateway has answered, null for none. `untouched`, where a row states it, is whether, when the client has closed, every key of `startupStorage` holds what it held and no other key under either prefix is there. `crossTab`: kb-a is active, its stored sign-in names jo, and its client, kept for jo, holds a value of res-1 it has not yet written; then another context writes kb-a's stored sign-in as `stored` says (null: deleted; otherwise a sign-in with other tokens whose personKey is the one stated, or which has none for null), and the client closes. `saved` is whether jo's `resource` key then holds the value the client held: a session that sees its stored sign-in deleted, or replaced by a sign-in that does not name its person, discards what it has not written, and writes nothing more; a renewal keeps the person, and changes nothing of what is written. Every runner runs all four parts and fails on a difference.

keys.why: a key with both characters base64url puts where base64 puts + and /, and no padding
another person on a knowledge base whose id is a UUID: the id is spelled as it is, and the person's key is their own

signOut.why: a knowledge base with no open client: every key of the person its sign-in names goes, and no other person's, nor theirs on another knowledge base
an open client is closed before anything is deleted, so nothing of the person is left, whatever its closing writes
a sign-in whose gateway never named its person: no key is known to be theirs, so none is deleted

startup.why: a sign-in that names its person: what was kept for them is read as the client is made, before the gateway answers
a sign-in that does not yet name its person keeps nothing until the gateway names them; then the sign-in records them, and what was kept for them is read and the stream's places restored
a gateway that names nobody: nothing is read, nothing is recorded, and nothing is written

crossTab.why: the stored sign-in deleted by another context: what was not written is discarded
a new sign-in in another context, whose gateway has not named its person: what was not written is discarded
another person signed in in another context: what was not written is discarded
a renewal in another context keeps the person: what was not written is written as the client closes
